The '''Embraer EMB-505 Phenom 300''' is a light [[business jet]] designed and produced by the [[Brazil]]ian aerospace manufacturer [[Embraer]]. Certified for single-pilot operations, it can carry up to 11 occupants.<ref>{{cite web |url = http://www.airweb.faa.gov/Regulatory_and_Guidance_Library/rgMakeModel.nsf/0/58049d55942d6fc486257e190072fbfc/$FILE/A60CE_Rev_9.pdf |title = Airweb/Embraer 300 |publisher = [[Federal Aviation Administration]] |access-date = 2 July 2023}}</ref> Work on the Phenom 300 started in response to customer demands for a larger business aircraft than the [[Embraer Phenom 100|Phenom 100]], a [[very light jet]]. While the design team originally intended for the aircraft to be a straightforward stretched derivative of the Phenom 100, a clean sheet approach was later adopted. The Phenom 300 featured more powerful engines, the addition of [[Spoiler (aeronautics)|spoiler]] and [[winglet]]s, along with an elongated cabin to accommodate more passengers. Several features, from its cabin and interior design to its [[landing gear]] and structure, can be traced back to the Phenom 100.

The prototype Phenom 300 conducted its [[maiden flight]] on 29 April 2008, [[type certification]] was received on 3 December 2009, permitting its entry into service that same month. In 2013, the Phenom 300 was the most delivered business jet. During March 2019, Embraer delivered the 500th Phenom 300, claiming more than half of the light jet market share since 2012. On 31 January 2020, Embraer announced that it was implementing a package of upgrades to the Phenom 300. Certification of the improved Phenom 300E was received during March 2020.

== Development ==
[[File:Embraer Phenom 300 Mockup.jpg|thumb|Scale model at [[ILA Berlin Air Show]] 2006]]

During the early 2000s, Embraer was in the process of designing the [[Embraer Phenom 100|Phenom 100]] light [[business jet]]; while conducting market research, it was discovered that numerous potential customers were expressing a desire for an enlarged model of the aircraft.<ref name="fg2008"/> Accordingly, in 2004, it was decided to produce a derivative of the Phenom 100, which the company designated as the ''Phenom 300''. Initial design work was focused on a straightforward scaling up of the Phenom 100, however, Embraer later concluded that a "clean sheet" approach was necessary, leading to the adoption of more powerful engines, [[Spoiler (aeronautics)|spoiler]]-equipped swept wings, and detachable aluminium [[winglet]]s.<ref name="fg2008"/> Various features from the Phenom 100 were transferred across, such as its relatively long structural life, an all-[[composite material|composite]] T-tail, trailing-link [[landing gear]], [[fly-by-wire]] brakes, the Prodigy avionics suite, a cabin and cockpit interior designed by [[Designworks|BMW DesignWorksUSA]].<ref name="fg2008"/>

On 29 April 2008, the prototype Phenom 300 conducted its [[maiden flight]], flown by John Sevalho Corção and Embraer's chief pilot Eduardo Alves Meni; this flight took place several months ahead of the original development schedule.<ref name="fg2008">{{Citation |last = Croft |first = John |title = Embraer Phenom 300: bolder big brother |date = 12 May 2008 |url = http://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/embraer-phenom-300-bolder-big-brother-223614/ |work = [[Flightglobal]] |access-date = 28 March 2015 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150328105617/http://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/embraer-phenom-300-bolder-big-brother-223614/ |url-status = live |publisher = Reed Business Information |archive-date = 28 March 2015}}</ref><ref name = "flightesting ain2008"/> On its second flight, made on 6 May, the prototype was flown from [[Gavião Peixoto]] to Embraer's headquarters at [[São José dos Campos]] for further evaluation. A total of three Phenom 300s flew roughly 1,400 hours in support of the certification programme.<ref name = "flightesting ain2008">{{cite web |url = https://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/aviation-international-news/2008-06-04/embraers-phenom-300-enters-flight-test-phase |title = Embraer's Phenom 300 enters flight-test phase |publisher = AIN Online |first = Matt |last = Thurber |date = 4 June 2008 |access-date = 2 July 2023 |archive-date = 2 July 2023 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20230702184647/https://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/aviation-international-news/2008-06-04/embraers-phenom-300-enters-flight-test-phase |url-status = dead }}</ref> On 3 December 2009, the Phenom 300 received its [[type certification]] from the [[Federal Aviation Administration]] (FAA).<ref name="fg2010">{{Citation |last = Gerzanics |first = Mike |title = FLIGHT TEST: Embraer Phenom 300 |date = 27 April 2010 |url = http://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/flight-test-embraer-phenom-300-341010/ |work = Flightglobal |access-date = 28 March 2015 |publisher = Reed Business Information}}</ref> On 29 December 2009, Embraer delivered the first Phenom 300 to Executive Flight Services at the company's headquarters at São José dos Campos, Brazil.<ref>{{Cite journal |date = 11 January 2010 |title = News Breaks: Embraer Delivers First Phenom 300 Light Jet |journal = Aviation Week |publisher = McGraw-Hill |page = 18}}</ref>

On 31 January 2020, Embraer announced that it was implementing a package of upgrades to the Phenom 300; resulting changes included the maximum speed being increased from Mach 0.78 to 0.80 ({{cvt|446 to 464|kn|disp=comma}}), expanded endurance from {{cvt|1,992 to 2,010|nmi}}, and the rated engine thrust being raised from {{cvt|3,360 to 3,478|lbf|kN}} via the adoption of improved PW535E1 turbofan engines.<ref name="AWST2020" /> During March 2020, the Phenom 300E received triple certification from Brazil's ANAC, the FAA, and EASA.<ref name = "AIN pilotreport2020"/> By early 2023, the aircraft's equipped price was {{US$|10.995 million}}.<ref>{{Cite news |date = Second Quarter 2023 |title = Purchase planning handbook – Jets table |work = Business & Commercial Aircraft |url = https://infogram.com/bca-table-2023-jets-1ho16vorwrp8x4n}}</ref>

== Design ==
[[File:Embraer Phenom 300 cabin, EBACE 2019.jpg|thumb|Club seating with recessed aisle]]
[[File:F-HJBR (31435863270).jpg|thumb|From below, showing its [[swept wing]]]]
[[File:Embraer 505 Phenom 300, Private JP7321031.jpg|thumb|[[Garmin G1000]] based flight deck]]
The Phenom 300 is a twin-engined [[cantilever]] [[monoplane]] with low-positioned swept wings. It is powered by a pair of [[Pratt & Whitney Canada PW500|Pratt & Whitney Canada PW535E]] [[turbofan]] engines that are mounted at the rear of the fuselage on pylons. The structure, which comprises 18% [[composite material]]s, has a rate lifespan of 28,000 flight cycles or 35,000 flight hours; it is considerably stronger than that of the Phenom 100 in part due to the aircraft's higher operating altitude.<ref name="fg2008" /> It was decided not to equip the Phenom 300 with [[thrust reverser]]s, instead relying on the use of [[fly-by-wire]] brakes with anti-skid protection incorporated.<ref name="fg2008" /> It also has retractable [[tricycle landing gear]]. Despite the aircraft's increased size, the Phenom 300 is capable of flying out of various smaller commuter airports, such as [[London City Airport|London City]] and [[Telluride Regional Airport]].<ref name="fg2008"/>

The cabin can accommodate up to nine passengers along with a two-pilot crew; an additional passenger can be carried when being flown by a single pilot. Optional cabin fittings include rotating seats and a two-person side-facing divan in lieu of the seventh seat in the front.<ref name="fg2008" /> The addition of a [[Galley (kitchen)|galley]] also comes at the cost of the seat opposite the entry door.<ref name = "AIN pilotreport2020"/> Access to the cockpit and cabin is via an [[airstair]] on the left-hand side. The Phenom 300 is equipped with an externally serviced private rear lavatory and is outfitted for [[single-point refueling]].<ref name="fg2010" /> For additional comfort, [[soundproofing]] is integrated along with the careful designing of various mechanical components to reduce noise generation.<ref name = "AIN pilotreport2020"/> It has an unpressurised cargo hold, large enough to hold six pairs of skis (or six golf bags), six roll-on bags, and six laptop bags.<ref name="fg2008" />

The cockpit of the Phenom 300 is equipped with three Garmin G1000 12in (305mm) [[liquid crystal display]]s, comprising a pair of flight displays and a single central multifunction display, along with traditional control yokes for the two pilots.<ref name="fg2008" /> An alphanumeric keypad is used to interact with the flight management system, communications and navigation radios. The aircraft is provisioned a Garmin GFC700 digital three-axis [[autopilot]] that has dual-channel "fail passive" functionality with roll, pitch and yaw control as well as automatic pitch trim and Mach trim.<ref name="fg2008" /> To reduce complexity and potential for confusion, mix-mode anti-icing measures were avoided in favour of exclusively using a variable [[bleed air]] system to heat both horizontal wings while permitting a safe level of ice to accrete on the vertical stabiliser. [[Electronic flight bag]]s are available as optional equipment.<ref name="fg2008" /> Later-built examples are equipped with the ''Prodigy Touch'' system.<ref name = "touch upgrade2014"/>

To better accommodate the cruise speed of the Phenom 300, which is noticeably higher than its Phenom 100 predecessor, a movable horizontal stabiliser in a [[T-tail]] configuration was adopted.<ref name="fg2008" /> Pilots are able to set different [[trim tab|trim]] positions for this movable tail to best suit take-off and cruise profiles, decreasing the amount of take-off "pull" needed to displace the [[Elevator (aeronautics)|elevator]] via the conventional cable and pulley controls, which are also used for the [[aileron]]s and [[rudder]]. Electrical actuation is used for the [[Flap (aeronautics)|flaps]], [[trim tab]]s, and autopilot operations.<ref name="fg2008" /> To mitigate the aircraft's tendency to [[Dutch roll]], a [[rudder]] on the ventral fin acts as a [[yaw damper]].<ref name=Flight9Feb2009>{{cite news |first = Mike |last = Gerzanics |title = Flight Test: Phenom 100 - building on a Legacy |url = https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/flight-test-phenom-100-building-on-a-legacy-322207/ |work = [[Flightglobal]] |date = 9 February 2009 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160816115845/https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/flight-test-phenom-100-building-on-a-legacy-322207/ |archive-date = 16 August 2016 |url-status = live }}</ref> Various avionics improvements have led to new functionality being added to later-built aircraft, such as predictive [[wind shear]] awareness, stabilized approach, emergency descent mode (in event of [[pressurized cabin|cabin depressurisation]]) and an in-house runway overrun awareness and alerting system (ROAAS).<ref name = "AIN pilotreport2020"/>

== Variants ==
[[File:Embraer Phenom 300 N310GV taxiing at Scottsdale Airport, October 2023.jpg|thumb|A Phenom 300 taxiing at [[Scottsdale Airport]] in Arizona, 2023]]
 <!-- linked from redirect [[Phenom 300E]] -->
;Phenom 300
: Original EMB-505 model, produced since 2009.

;Phenom 300E
: In 2018, Embraer launched an upgraded model of Phenom, featuring a redesigned interior, new avionics suite (Garmin-G3000-based Prodigy Touch), and a Ground Power Mode for the engines.<ref>{{Cite magazine |title = A Look Inside the Phenom 300E |url = https://www.flyingmag.com/look-inside-embraer-phenom-300e/ |magazine =  Flying |first = Rob |last = Mark |date = 22 January 2019}}</ref>

;2020 Phenom 300E
: An upgraded Phenom 300E was announced in 2020, featuring upgraded PW535E1 engines, with thrust increased to 3,478 lbf (from 3,360 lbf); maximum speed has increased to Mach 0.80 from 0.78 (464 vs. 446 kn), and range increased from {{cvt|1992|to|2010|nmi}}.<ref name="AWST2020" /> Avionics improvements include predictive wind shear awareness, stabilized approach, and an Embraer-developed runway overrun awareness and alerting system (ROAAS).<ref name = "AIN pilotreport2020">{{cite web |url = https://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/business-aviation/2020-04-07/pilot-report-embraers-new-phenom-300e |title = Pilot Report: Embraer's New Phenom 300E |publisher = AIN Online |first = Matt |last = Thurber |date = 7 April 2020}}</ref> In addition, Bossa Nova interior option became available.<ref name="AWST2020" />

;2020 Phenom 300MED
: A ready-fit [[medevac]] configuration was made available in August 2020 for new-build aircraft. This program also allows existing Phenom 300s to be retrofitted with a medevac interior.<ref>{{Cite web |date = 23 October 2020 |title = A Comprehensive Review of the Phenom 300 |publisher = Elliott Jets |url = https://www.elliottjets.com/a-comprehensive-review-of-the-phenom-300/}}</ref>

== Deliveries ==
In 2013, the Phenom 300 was the most delivered business jet, with 60 units.<ref>{{Cite news |last = Sarsfield |first = Kate |date = 29 December 2014 |title = NetJets converts Phenom 300 options into firm orders |publisher = Flightglobal |url = https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/netjets-converts-phenom-300-options-into-firm-orders-407496/ |access-date = 30 December 2014}}</ref> It also led the industry in deliveries in 2014 and 2015.<ref>{{Cite press release |title = Embraer Phenom 300 is most-delivered business jet in the world for the third consecutive year |date = 23 February 2016 |publisher = Embraer |url = http://www.embraer.com.br/en-us/imprensaeventos/press-releases/noticias/pages/embraer-phenom-300-is-most-delivered-business-jet-in-the-world-for-the-third-consecutive-year.aspx}}</ref>

After July 2016, all Phenom assembly was transferred to the [[Melbourne, Florida]] line, which has the capability to assemble 96 Phenoms and 72 [[Embraer Legacy 450]]/[[Embraer Legacy 500]]s annually.<ref>{{Cite news |first = Chad |last = Trautvetter |date = 2 June 2016 |title = Embraer Starts Legacy 450/500 Production in US |publisher = Aviation International News |url = http://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/business-aviation/2016-06-02/embraer-starts-legacy-450/500-production-us?eid=343244824&bid=1422224 |access-date = 3 June 2016 |archive-date = 11 June 2016 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160611125659/http://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/business-aviation/2016-06-02/embraer-starts-legacy-450/500-production-us?eid=343244824&bid=1422224 |url-status = dead }}</ref> More than 170 Phenom jets had been produced at the site by June 2016, mainly for the US market.<ref>{{Cite news |date = 8 June 2016 |title = Embraer opens Legacy final assembly facility in Melbourne |publisher = Flight International |url = https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/embraer-opens-legacy-final-assembly-facility-in-melb-426151/}}</ref>

In March 2019, Embraer delivered the 500th Phenom 300, claiming more than half of the light jet market share since 2012; at the time it was being used in over 30 countries and had cumulative carried 2.5 million passengers across 600,000 flights and 800,000 hours.<ref name="Embraer25mar2019">{{Cite press release |title = Embraer delivers the 500th Phenom 300 series aircraft, the most successful business jet of the decade |date = 25 March 2019 |publisher = Embraer |url = https://embraer.com/global/en/news?slug=1206549-embraer-delivers-the-500th-phenom-300-series-aircraft-the-most-successful-business-jet-of-the-decade}}</ref> As of February 2023, 700 units have been delivered.<ref name= "700th unit">{{cite web |url = https://www.aviationpros.com/aircraft/business-general-aviation/press-release/53026369/embraer-embraers-phenom-300-becomes-worlds-best-selling-light-jet-for-11th-consecutive-year|title = Embraer's Phenom 300 Becomes World's Best-Selling Light Jet for 11th Consecutive Year |date = 23 February 2023 |publisher = aviationpro |access-date = 23 January 2024}}</ref>

== Accidents and incidents ==
As of January 2023, the Phenom 300 has been involved in three [[hull-loss]] accidents causing five fatalities.<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 May 2020 |title=Embraer Phenom 300 Statistics |url=https://aviation-safety.net/database/types/Embraer-Phenom-300/statistics |publisher=[[Aviation Safety Network]]}}</ref>

* On 10 January 2011, a Phenom 300 operated by the [[Royal Oman Police]] registered as A4O-CY made an [[emergency landing]] on [[Muscat International Airport]] with the right-main landing gear indication not down and locked position, shortly after landing the right main-gear collapsed and subsequently the aircraft banked to the right which caused the right-wing tip to come into contact with the runway surface. All 8 occupants on board survived.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://asn.flightsafety.org/wikibase/502133 |title=Embraer EMB-505 Phenom 300 : Aviation Safety Report|website=Asn.flightsafety.org|access-date=September 18, 2026}}</ref>
* On 31 July 2015, a Phenom 300, [[aircraft registration]] ''HZ-IBN'', [[2015 Blackbushe Phenom 300 crash|crashed into a car park]] whilst trying to land at [[Blackbushe Airport]] in Hampshire. All four persons on board the Saudi-registered private jet died in the crash and subsequent fire.<ref>{{Cite news |date=31 July 2015 |title=Blackbushe Airport: Four dead in car auction site plane crash |work=[[BBC News]] |publisher=[[BBC]] |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-surrey-33736685}}</ref>
* On 2 January 2023, Phenom 300 ''N555NR'' crashed shortly after takeoff on the grounds of [[Provo Municipal Airport]] in Utah. The pilot was killed, one passenger was critically injured, and the two other passengers received minor injuries.<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 January 2023 |title=Top Nu Skin distributor killed in plane crash at Provo Airport |url=https://www.deseret.com/utah/2023/1/3/23537734/nathan-ricks-nu-skin-killed-in-plane-crash-provo-airport |access-date=3 January 2023 |website=Deseret News |language=en}}</ref> On April 24, 2025, the NTSB released the final report on the incident, citing icing conditions present at the time, along with the crew's failure to use available deicing resources, activate onboard anti-icing equipment, and perform the visual inspection of the flight surfaces mandated under the weather conditions as the probable cause of the accident.  This led to a nearly immediate aerodynamic stall and left roll on takeoff ending in the uncontrolled impact with the terrain.<ref>{{Cite report |url=https://data.ntsb.gov/carol-repgen/api/Aviation/ReportMain/GenerateNewestReport/106520/pdf |title=Aviation Investigation Final Report |last=Cawthra |first=Joshua |date=April 24, 2025 |issue=WPR23FA080 |access-date=August 9, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>
